# Golden digests of the dense-linear workload's output: a tripwire, not an
# oracle (docs/verification.md §4). CRC-32 (core/crc32.hpp) of unit 0's output
# at seed 1, by kind of path and panel depth.
#
#   scalar  the scalar kernel: the same bits on x86-64 and on AArch64.
#   fused   the AVX2 kernel on x86-64 and the NEON kernel on AArch64: both
#           take fma(a, b, p) in increasing k from +0.0 (panel.hpp), so both
#           give these bits.
#
# Produced by tests/determinism/workloads/dense_linear/determinism_test.cpp,
# which prints every line it computes:
#
#   build/debug/tests/determinism/workloads/dense_linear/loadforge_determinism_workloads_dense_linear_tests \
#     --gtest_filter='*Digest*'
#
# on 2026-10-20 11:14 UTC, on an x86-64 Intel Xeon @ 2.10GHz (GCC 13.3,
# debug preset), giving the scalar and the fused (avx2) lines below; and the
# same test cross-built with aarch64-linux-gnu-g++-13 and run under
# qemu-aarch64 8.2 gave the identical scalar and fused (neon) lines. CI's
# ARM64 runner checks the AArch64 half on real hardware on every run.
#
# A change to these lines is a change to the bits the workload produces, which
# also changes the workload's version (kVersion, spec.hpp: a contract change)
# and is reviewed as such.
scalar 16 af65c959
scalar 32 7bc6feea
scalar 64 2ebcc7ae
scalar 128 a5e38cda
scalar 256 d39a845a
fused 16 0ecdcd89
fused 32 682c5b86
fused 64 65d62005
fused 128 5c5a33cf
